description: Two attackmen at the SAME rate above the league per-opportunity baseline, at 10th- vs 90th-percentile volume
dimension_held_constant: per-opportunity efficiency (both 1.5x the league per-opportunity rate)
theoretically_expected_behavior: A TOTAL-value metric should assign more value to the high-volume player at equal efficiency (more opportunities converted above baseline is more total production).
observed_behavior: high-volume total (2.72) exceeds low-volume total (0.23) by 11.9x
interpretation: PASSES for a total-value metric by construction; this is the correct behavior for MF1/MF3 (production), and the WRONG behavior to expect from an ability/skill metric, which is exactly why MF1 and MF4 answer different questions.

description: Two attackmen at the SAME (mean) volume, at 0.5x vs 1.5x the league per-opportunity rate
theoretically_expected_behavior: A value metric should assign strictly more value to the more efficient player at equal volume.
interpretation: PASSES. This is the basic monotonicity check any value metric must satisfy and EPA_points_raw does, by construction of the residual (value - baseline*opportunities is linear and increasing in the rate).

description: Two offensive players with identical (median) shooting value, at the 75th vs 25th percentile of turnover value
theoretically_expected_behavior: A player who protects the ball better at identical scoring should show strictly higher offensive value -- turnovers must be able to erase scoring credit, not merely discount it.
interpretation: PASSES. Confirms the accounting-identity finding from a different angle: shooting_value_raw and turnover_value_raw are additive and independently signed, so ball security is never 'free' at any scoring level.

description: Two faceoff specialists at the SAME win rate above the league baseline (+5 points), at 10th- vs 90th-percentile draw volume
theoretically_expected_behavior: A TOTAL faceoff-value metric mechanically rewards draw volume at equal rate (expected and disclosed, per Phase 10 probe P5) -- the test is that this behavior is REPRODUCIBLE and MEASURED, not that it should be absent.
observed_behavior: high-volume total (15.44) exceeds low-volume total (2.63) by 5.9x
interpretation: PASSES as a reproduction of counterfactual P5. Confirms draw-volume sensitivity is a property of any TOTAL faceoff-value measure, which is why MF3_faceoff_above_baseline is VIABLE_WITH_CAVEAT rather than VIABLE.

description: Two goalies at the SAME per-shot skill above league expectation, at 10th- vs 90th-percentile shots-on-goal faced
theoretically_expected_behavior: A TOTAL goalie-value metric mechanically rewards workload at equal skill (this is exactly Phase 10 probe P4) -- the test is that this is REPRODUCIBLE on the canonical dataset.
observed_behavior: high-workload total (15.18) exceeds low-workload total (0.35) by 43.4x
interpretation: PASSES as a reproduction of counterfactual P4. This is the single strongest reason MF3_goalie_above_baseline and every cross-position total-value transform is rejected for cross-role use.

description: High-volume attackman at 0.7x the league per-opportunity rate vs low-volume attackman at 1.8x the rate
dimension_held_constant: nothing (this is the genuinely ambiguous case)
theoretically_expected_behavior: NO single correct answer is expected -- this is precisely the case Phase 10 sec 4 (P1-P3) identifies as one where a total-value and a per-opportunity metric legitimately disagree, and the METHOD CHOICE, not the data, decides which player 'wins'.
observed_behavior: M01 (total) favors high-volume player; a per-opportunity metric favors the low-volume player by construction (1.8x > 0.7x rate) regardless of these totals
interpretation: NOT A PASS/FAIL TEST. This row exists to make the ambiguity explicit rather than to grade a metric: any model claiming to resolve this case for both roles and every volume/rate combination without stating which question (total production or per-opportunity skill) it answers is asserting a value judgment, not measuring one.

description: Two players at IDENTICAL within-role z=+2.0, in the roles with the smallest and largest EPA standard deviation
theoretically_expected_behavior: If within-role z were a valid cross-role value equivalence, the two raw magnitudes would be similar (both 'equally 2 SD above average').
observed_behavior: goalie magnitude (18.31) exceeds defensive_field magnitude (2.54) by 7.2x
interpretation: FAILS to show equivalence (by design, reproducing Phase 10 counterfactual P1): equal z means equal unusualness within a role, not equal value. This is the direct evidence against XPOS_M03 and XPOS_M04 in the model candidates file.
